title: S-meandric Permutations and Tangency Polynomials
summary: A meander is a configuration of two simple plane curves intersecting transversely. The orders of their intersection points define a permutation that determines the configuration. When tangencies are allowed, however, different configurations can share the same permutation. We study the combinatorial and algebraic structures arising from this non-uniqueness. We give a realization criterion and show that the realizations of each realizable permutation form an affine space over the two-element field.
